test_title: PYST 18: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question:
The marks obtained by the students of a class are given. Find the standard deviation of the marks (rounded off to 2 decimal places).

 65, 47, 59, 75, 82, 91, 55 and 78
solution:
**Given:**

Marks obtained: 65, 47, 59, 75, 82, 91, 55, 78

**Formula used:**

Standard deviation (σ) = sqrt{dfrac{sum (x_i - mu)²}{n}}

Where: μ = Mean, xᵢ = Individual values, n = Number of values

**Calculations:**

μ = dfrac{65+47+59+75+82+91+55+78}{8}

⇒ μ = dfrac{552}{8} = 69

Deviation (xi - μ) and square of deviation

(65 - 69)² = (-4)² = 16

(47 - 69)² = (-22)² = 484

(59 - 69)² = (-10)² = 100

(75 - 69)² = (6)² = 36

(82 - 69)² = (13)² = 169

(91 - 69)² = (22)² = 484

(55 - 69)² = (-14)² = 196

(78 - 69)² = (9)² = 81

Sum of squared deviations

sum (x - bar{x})² = 16 + 484 + 100 + 36 + 169 + 484 + 196 + 81 = 1566

Variance σ² = frac{sum (x - bar{x})²}{N} = (1566)/(8) = 195.75

Standard Deviation σ = sqrt{195.75}

⇒ σ ≈ 13.991068... ≈ 13.99

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**
